nodes.summary: The characteristic function of a set $p$ of natural numbers is the partial function $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$ that is defined at every $n$, with value $1$ if $n \in p$ and value $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Characteristic function of a set of naturals

nodes.summary: A set $p$ of natural numbers is decidable (computable as a predicate) if and only if its characteristic function is partial recursive.
nodes.title: A set is decidable iff its characteristic function is partial recursive

nodes.summary: Fix the standard bijective numbering $n \mapsto c_n$ of the codes of partial recursive functions $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$. The halting set is the set of natural numbers $n$ such that the partial recursive function with code $c_n$ is defined at $0$.
nodes.title: Halting set

nodes.summary: There is no computable function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n$, $n$ is outside the halting set if and only if $f(n)$ is in the halting set.
nodes.title: The complement of the halting set is not many-one reducible to it

nodes.summary: For every decidable set $q$ of natural numbers, the characteristic function of the halting set is not Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$.
nodes.title: The halting set is not Turing reducible to a decidable set

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be sets of natural numbers such that the characteristic function of $p$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$. If $q$ is decidable, then $p$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Decidability transfers down Turing reducibility

nodes.summary: For every set $p$ of natural numbers, the characteristic function of the complement $\mathbb{N} \setminus p$ and the characteristic function of $p$ are Turing equivalent: each is Turing reducible to the other.
nodes.title: Every set is Turing equivalent to its complement

nodes.summary: If $p$ and $q$ are sets of natural numbers and $p$ is many-one reducible to $q$, that is, there is a computable $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $n \in p \iff f(n) \in q$ for all $n$, then the characteristic function of $p$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$.
nodes.title: Many-one reducibility implies Turing reducibility

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
